verdicts.note: First-term incumbent, 2025 board chair, on the WSAC leadership track (S1, S2). Run on record and relationships. One term keeps it at -1; high is fine because S1 and S2 both document it.

Attacked toward -1. His statements are hedged: 'I do not believe simply raising taxes is the answer' and 'rather than relying solely on increased taxes' (S2). But he reports voting 'No' on seeking relief from the property tax cap (S3), and pole_a names levy-cap lifts explicitly. He also said he would work on the budget 'without raising taxes for citizens' (S7). A recorded position against a cap lift plus three statements across three sources supports -2. Medium confidence correctly reflects that the vote is his own account, with no independent record of it.

'The relationships that I've built' (S5), partnerships with cities and the Port (S1), and 'taking the fight to the legislators' through the counties' association (S6) fit pole_a's working within existing structures. No party or endorsement inference is used. Medium is right: this is a governing style, not a stated position on PAC money, term limits or similar.
S2 supports faster permitting through new software and removing state barriers that make it 'difficult and expensive' to build. This is pole_a's 'streamline permitting'. One source, so -1 medium.

A charter-county vote (direct democracy on the form of government), fewer elected offices, a pay cut and a personal two-term limit (S1, S2, S3) are squarely pole_b. The county GOP declined to endorse him because the platform 'does not align with the traditional Republican platform' (S2), which reinforces that he is running against existing structures. +2 high holds.

Attacked toward +1. He served two terms on the Columbia (Burbank) School Board (S1, S3), so he is not a pure outsider, and Reeves (auditor, never elected) got only +1. But Woody's whole campaign is anti-incumbency and pro-renewal: 'I am not a politician' (S1), a two-term limit, 'hopefully only one' (S1, S2), and a pay cut (S3). The axis describes the case the candidate makes, so +2 stands. Basis wording: the quoted phrase 'not a career politician' appears only in the contest dossier's paraphrase (S1, S4). The candidate dossier quotes S1 as 'I am not a politician'. Consider quoting that instead.

A zero-based review of every department and contract and 'a structural problem, not a revenue problem' (S4), plus about $200,000-$225,000 a year in salary savings from the charter (S1, S2, S3), make the fullest pole_a case in the race. Fix the basis: it says '152% revenue growth', but S4 as the dossier records it says 'the county budget has grown 152% since 2008'. That is budget growth, not revenue growth.
'Not a revenue problem' (S4) implies opposing new revenue, but he makes no explicit tax pledge and has no recorded vote. -1 medium is calibrated correctly against Fulmer's -2.

Attacked toward -2. S3 and S4 together support it: drop permits such as those for windows, longer permit-office hours and more online permits, 'hold the line on any new regulations', and 'getting government out of the way'. That is close to the full pole_a case. But nothing in the dossier addresses housing supply, rent regulation or public housing directly, so -1 medium is defensible and is not adjusted.
